// Part: room: parlour library (interior designer + lamplighter). Inner air x27..43 x z43..49, floor y4, ceiling y9.
// Layout (origin [27,4,43], rows along +z, 17 columns along +x):
//   - bookshelf wall on the west (x27) and north (z43) walls, the windows' cells in front of them kept clear
//   - focal: the reading group in front of the east face of the chimney stack (x33..34 z46..47): a table with
//     two stair chairs, a candle on the table, a red carpet under it
//   - a second reading table with two chairs in the west nook, a lectern by the front window
//   - a barrel in the south-west corner; the hall door (x44 z46..47) and the corridor doors (z50) stay clear
//   - two hanging lanterns from iron_chain on the ceiling (lamplighter)
import { layers } from "/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs";
import { porchLantern } from "../vocab.mjs";

const LEGEND = {
  B: "bookshelf",
  r: "red_carpet",
  f: "dark_oak_fence",
  T: ["dark_oak_slab", { type: "top" }],
  W: ["dark_oak_stairs", { facing: "west", half: "bottom" }],
  E: ["dark_oak_stairs", { facing: "east", half: "bottom" }],
  L: ["lectern", { facing: "east" }],
  h: "barrel",
  k: ["candle", { candles: "2", lit: "true" }],
  g: ["lantern", { hanging: "false" }],
};

// y4: floor furniture (bookshelves, carpet, tables and chairs, lectern, barrel)
const Y4 = [
  "B  BBBB  BBBB  BB", // z43
  "BL               ", // z44
  "  g     rrrrr    ", // z45
  "  WfE   rrWfEr   ", // z46
  "B       rrrgrr   ", // z47
  "B       rrrrr    ", // z48
  "h                ", // z49
];

// y5: second tier of bookshelves, and the two table tops (top slabs)
const Y5 = [
  "B  BBBB  BBBB  BB", // z43
  "B                ", // z44
  "                 ", // z45
  "   T       T     ", // z46
  "B                ", // z47
  "B                ", // z48
  "                 ", // z49
];

// y6: a standing lantern on the west table, a lit candle on the east one
const Y6 = [
  "                 ",
  "                 ",
  "                 ",
  "   g       k     ",
  "                 ",
  "                 ",
  "                 ",
];

export function build(g) {
  layers(g, [27, 4, 43], LEGEND, [Y4, Y5, Y6]);
  // lamplighter: two hanging lanterns on chains under the upper floor, over the reading groups
  porchLantern(g, 31, 9, 45);
  porchLantern(g, 39, 9, 48);
}

input.summary:
Parlour library (room-2) is not built: all 64 of its non-air writes are refused, so it places nothing and make.sh only writes build.nbt without its furniture.
The cause is in the shell, not in room-2.mjs: shell.mjs:27 fills every room interior with "air", and runParts locks air too, so every room cell is owned by an earlier part.
room-2.mjs has no off-palette blocks and I left it unchanged; the fix belongs in shell.mjs or runParts, which I was told not to edit.

waste.what: Working out why room-2 was refused: reading shell.mjs and the runParts lock to find that the shell's box() fill (shell.mjs:27) and the partition and doorway carves own every room cell.
waste.cost: about 3 tool calls and two large source reads (roughly 15k tokens) to reach a conclusion the report could state in one line.
waste.tool: runParts could name the owning part for each refused cell (e.g. 'owned by mansion shell: carved air') and warn when a part's footprint has zero free cells, so the error is flagged at the shell rather than as 64 refusals in room-2.

waste.what: Counting the room-2 writes to confirm the refusals matched the whole footprint. The report keeps only the first 8 refused cells, so I counted the layers by hand (about 59 layer cells plus the two porch lanterns).
waste.cost: one hand count across three layers and two lanterns; no retries.
waste.tool: parts-report.json could keep the full refused list, or give per-part counts of refused cells grouped by owner, so the total is read rather than reconstructed.

companions.task: Own the shell's wall and partition layout in shell.mjs. Ask them to stop carving room interiors to air (box() at line 27, plus the partition and doorway carves) so only walls, floors and openings are locked, and room cells stay free for furnishing. Room-2's 64 writes should then go through without edits.
After the lock is lifted, check room-2's built-in joinery: the two stair chairs, the lectern and the bookshelf wall fit the window and door clearances in the plan's rooms.json.

left: Blocker, shared with every room part: the shell (shell.mjs:27 and the carves at lines 27-120) fills all room interiors with air, so runParts counts them as owned. Every room part reports 0 placed (for example 'room: entrance hall: 0 placed'), not only room-2. A mason or whoever owns shell.mjs must stop locking room interiors, or runParts must stop treating air as owned.
Once unblocked, room-2 must be re-run through ./make.sh; I have not verified that all 64 writes pass, since the lock is what refuses them.
No OFF-PALETTE issue in room-2; every block it uses (bookshelf, red_carpet, dark_oak_fence/stairs/slab, lectern, barrel, candle, lantern, iron_chain) is in palette.json.

Observation for the roofs part: parts-report.json lists off-palette blocks from roof.json (tuff_bricks, cobbled_deepslate_stairs, polished_deepslate_slab and others), reported under the mansion shell. This is not room-2's problem.
